claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl powder with a 15–45 μm particle-size range is the initial feedstock.
Standard HVAF-i7 processing of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces coatings of acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
Reducing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance will increase particle velocity.
Increasing particle velocity by adjusting gas pressure is equivalent to reducing nozzle standoff distance for the proposed intervention.
Higher particle velocity will increase impact kinetic energy.
Higher particle velocity and impact energy will improve particle flattening.
Improved particle flattening will strengthen inter-splat bonding.
Improved momentum transfer during particle impact will produce a denser coating with lower porosity.
Increasing particle impact energy will reduce inter-particle oxidation.
The proposed intervention will boost deposition efficiency.
The proposed intervention will increase FeCoNiCrAl coating thickness relative to the standard HVAF-i7 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline.
The thickness increase can be achieved without significantly compromising coating integrity or oxidation resistance.
The intervention can remain effective during low-temperature ID-HVAF deposition inside diameters as small as 120 mm.
Coatings produced using the intervention can remain effective under elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions.
Excessive particle energy may cause overheating, oxidation, or microstructural defects.
